metaTitle: Best Winix Air Purifiers, Lineup Compared (2026)
metaDescription: Winix air purifiers compared across the A230, 5500, T800 and 9800 lines, with verified room sizes, WiFi differences and PlasmaWave explained.
expertTake: The Winix 5520 is the top pick because it combines a verified 392 square foot room size with True HEPA, carbon and an air quality monitor. The A230 is the value pick for a bedroom. Anyone who wants the quietest possible bedroom machine should compare decibel figures elsewhere, because this lineup is built for airflow and verified sizing first.
introParagraphs: One maker's purifiers often look interchangeable in a search result, with similar names and a string of model numbers. In reality the differences come down to room size, how the unit connects and which extra filtering stages it adds, and the model numbers hide all three.

This guide sorts a single maker's lineup by honest room size, then by connectivity and by the extras that change ownership. Every unit here states its coverage the same way, which makes comparison easy, and the sections below show how to read those numbers.

products.name: Winix 5520 True HEPA with monitor, verified at 392 sq ft
products.description:
The 5520 is the clearest example of how this lineup states its coverage. A verified room size of 392 square feet, a one-hour figure of 1,882 and a half-hour figure of 941 are all the same airflow expressed at different air-change rates, so you can read off the room it handles at the allergy-grade rate directly. That is a rare level of transparency.

The filter stack is a fine mesh pre-filter, a True HEPA layer and a carbon filter for VOCs and odors from cooking, pets and smoke, and an air quality monitor drives the auto mode. The listing claims 99.99 percent capture, a brand claim above the standard 99.97 percent, so read it as a True HEPA filter with a generous figure.

Compared with the 5510, it adds the air quality monitor and drops the app, and the 5530 sits alongside it with app control. Ownership is a replacement of the HEPA and carbon set, a pre-filter vacuum and a clear space around the intake. Genuine filters are easy to source. In practice the 392 square foot figure means a 16 by 24 foot living room is about the largest space it should be asked to handle at full allergy-grade performance, and anything bigger is better served by the 9800. The monitor is useful during cooking, when the display climbs and the auto mode raises the fan, then settles when the air clears.
products.bestFor: Living rooms near 390 square feet that want a monitor and no app.
pros: Coverage stated at three air-change rates
True HEPA with a carbon odor stage
Air quality monitor drives auto mode
cons: Louder than bedroom units at full speed

products.name: Winix 5510 True HEPA with carbon and app support
products.description:
The 5510 is the new generation of the 5500-2 with app support, and it shares the 5520's core: a verified 392 square foot room, a one-hour figure near 1,881 and a True HEPA and carbon filter. The difference is the app, which adds scheduling and monitoring.

The listing makes the same 99.99 percent capture claim and includes a carbon filter that reduces VOCs and household odors. Because the airflow is the same, the choice between the 5510 and the 5520 is purely about control: an app or a built-in monitor.

Ownership is the same filter set and mesh pre-filter. The 5530 is a further variant with app control, and the three together form one family. Pick on features, not on airflow. If you already own the older 5500-2, the main reason to upgrade is the app, since the filtering hardware is the same family. A scheduled quiet period overnight and a stronger run while you are out is the most practical use of the app, and it costs nothing in airflow.
products.bestFor: Rooms near 390 square feet where app scheduling matters.
cons: No air quality monitor on the listing

products.name: Winix T810 smart purifier, verified at 410 sq ft
products.description:
The T810 steps up to a verified 410 square foot room and a one-hour figure of 1,968 square feet, which is the same ratio of about 4.8 air changes at the verified size. It adds smart WiFi control that lets you monitor and control the unit from anywhere.

A fine mesh pre-filter protects a True HEPA layer, and the listing claims 99.99 percent capture. The extra 18 square feet over the 5500 series is small, so the case for the T810 is the T-series design and the WiFi, not a different class of room.

Ownership is a filter set swap and a pre-filter vacuum. Compared with the T830, it is the earlier version in the same size class. The T-series pairs well with a household that already uses a smart home hub, and the half-hour figure of 984 square feet is useful when guests arrive and you want a fast pass. Keep the mesh pre-filter vacuumed monthly, since a larger fan pulls more dust through it.
products.bestFor: Larger rooms near 410 square feet with WiFi control.
pros: True HEPA with a mesh pre-filter
cons: Only a small step above the 5500 series

products.name: Winix T830 smart purifier with air quality monitor
products.description:
The T830 shares the T810's verified 410 square foot room and adds an air quality monitor to the smart WiFi control. It is the unit in this lineup with both an on-device monitor and an app, so it works well whether or not you use the phone.

The filter stack is the same fine mesh pre-filter and True HEPA layer, with the 99.99 percent listing claim. The T830 is aimed at extra large rooms, and its one-hour figure is 1,968 square feet.

Ownership is the same filter set. Compared with the 5520, it has more room and an app, and a higher tier. The monitor makes it easy to see the effect of opening a window or running the stove, and the app logs the history. Because the T830 and T810 share their airflow, the difference between them is purely the on-device display, so choose on whether you want one.
products.bestFor: Extra large rooms near 410 square feet that want a monitor and WiFi.
pros: True HEPA with a mesh pre-filter
cons: Smart features rely on the cloud

products.name: Winix A230 bedroom purifier, verified at 230 sq ft
products.description:
The A230 is the bedroom unit, with a verified room size of 230 square feet, a one-hour figure of 1,110 and a half-hour figure of 555. A 230 square foot rating fits a bedroom or an office exactly, which is why it is the pick for that class.

It carries a True HEPA filter listed at 99.97 percent, a carbon filter for odors and an air quality monitor with auto mode. The listing is the most modest of the lineup, which suits the room it targets.

Ownership is a filter set and a clear intake. Next to the 5520, it has about 60 percent of the verified room, and a smaller footprint. A 230 square foot rating is about a 12 by 19 foot room, which covers most bedrooms. If your bedroom is larger, or you want to cover a connected hall, the 5520 gives you the next step. The A230 is the quietest in the family at low speed, and its footprint is the smallest, so it is the one to place on the floor beside a dresser.
products.bestFor: Bedrooms and offices near 230 square feet.
pros: True HEPA at the standard 99.97 percent
Air quality monitor with auto mode

products.name: Winix 9800 4-stage True HEPA with WiFi and PlasmaWave
products.description:
The 9800 is the largest unit here, with a verified room size of 500 square feet and a one-hour figure of 2,420. It is a four-stage design with a washable fine mesh pre-filter, a True HEPA layer and WiFi control.

It also carries PlasmaWave, the maker's ionization-style stage, which is the part to treat with caution. Ionization-type stages can produce small amounts of ozone, so look for a CARB certification or a low-ozone statement on the listing, and check whether the stage can be switched off. The filtering itself does not need it.

Ownership is a washable pre-filter and a filter swap. It is the pick for a large open space where the verified room matters. At 500 verified square feet it is the machine to choose for a large open room, a basement or a studio. Its washable mesh pre-filter is the chore to remember, and the filter set is the larger cost. Because it is the older design in the family, compare it with the T830 before you buy.
products.bestFor: Large rooms near 500 square feet that want a verified rating.
pros: Four stages with a washable pre-filter
cons: PlasmaWave stage should be checked for ozone statements
Older design than the T series

buyingCriteria.explanation: Each listing gives a verified room size, a one-hour figure and a half-hour figure. The verified size is the allergy-grade room, about one fifth of the one-hour number. The 5520's 392 square feet and the A230's 230 are the figures to size against. The maker's three-rate format is unusually helpful, because the half-hour number lets you see how quickly the unit can clear a room after a spike.

The 5510, 5520 and 5530 share the same verified 392 square foot airflow and differ in app and monitor. Pay for the control style you want and not for a different class of room. The T810 and T830 are a similar pair at 410 square feet. A buyer who spends extra for the 5530 over the 5520 should do it only if they want the app.
A built-in air quality monitor, as on the 5520 and A230, works without a phone. WiFi, as on the 5510, T810 and 9800, adds scheduling and remote control. The T830 has both.

The listings claim 99.99 percent capture for most models and 99.97 percent for the A230. The standard True HEPA figure is 99.97 percent at 0.3 microns, so the higher number is a brand claim and not a higher grade. Do not choose on the difference.

The 9800 includes PlasmaWave, an ionization-style stage. Ionizers can emit ozone, so look for CARB certification or a low-ozone statement, and check whether the stage can be switched off. Filtration does not depend on it.
The 9800 lists a washable fine mesh pre-filter, which lowers running cost. The others use a mesh pre-filter that vacuums clean. Either way, keep the first stage clean to protect the HEPA layer.

howWeEvaluated.title: Verified room size
howWeEvaluated.description: We placed each model by its verified room size and checked the one-hour figure for consistency, since the ratio is about 4.8. The lineup spans 230 to 500 square feet. This is a spec-sheet review.

howWeEvaluated.title: Controls
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared apps, monitors and WiFi across the models. The 5520 and A230 use monitors, the 5510, T810 and 9800 use WiFi, and the T830 has both.

howWeEvaluated.title: Filter stack
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at pre-filters, True HEPA claims and carbon stages, and flagged the PlasmaWave stage on the 9800.

howWeEvaluated.title: Family overlap
howWeEvaluated.description: Because several models share the same airflow, we ranked on features and not on airflow. This is why the 5510, 5520 and 5530 are discussed together even though only some are ranked.

howWeEvaluated.title: Supply
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked that genuine filters are easy to find, a strength of an established maker.

faq.q: Which Winix is best for a bedroom?
faq.a: The A230, verified at 230 square feet, fits a bedroom or office. If the bedroom is larger than 300 square feet, step up to the 5520.

faq.q: What is the difference between the 5510, 5520 and 5530?
faq.a: They share the same verified 392 square foot airflow. The 5520 has an air quality monitor, and the 5510 and 5530 add app support. Check the product title for the exact model, since the names are close.
Ionization-type stages can produce small amounts of ozone. Look for CARB certification or a low-ozone statement, and check whether you can switch it off.

faq.q: How do I read the coverage numbers?
faq.a: The verified room size is the honest allergy-grade room. The one-hour figure is about five times that, and the half-hour figure about 2.5 times. For a room that sits between two sizes, choose the larger.
No. The monitor models work well without it. WiFi adds scheduling and remote control.

faq.q: How often do filters need replacing?
faq.a: About once a year for many households, sooner with pets or smoke. Use genuine filters.
